collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — PONDERING HOW LIFE HAS GONE (LIF-01..50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Adults of every age looking at their own lives so far: roads not taken, quiet satisfaction, small regrets, unexpected pride, things left unfinished, luck, gratitude and plenty of amusement. Nobody has to reach a verdict.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

collection.description: At the festival, a villager is too old to dance all night and too young for the elders' log: dance, or sit with the elders.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: At the festival, the young people are dancing wildly by the fire, and the elders are sitting in a row on the log, watching and commenting. (name1) is standing between them, not quite sure which way to go. (He/she) is too old to dance all night and too young to sit on the elders' log. (He/she) is, (he/she) realizes, in the middle.

o1__fx.name: Outcome A
o1__fx.text: (name1) dances. For a while, at least. (He/she) is out of breath much sooner than (he/she) used to be, but (he/she) has better moves than (he/she) remembered. Then (he/she) sits on the end of the elders' log for a rest. The elders shift to make room. Nobody says anything. (name1) decides the middle is the best place to be: you get to do both.

o2__fx.name: Outcome B
o2__fx.text: (name1) sits on the end of the log. The elders welcome (him/her) with a nod. The commentary is excellent: who's dancing with whom, who's going to fall over next, who used to dance exactly like that in their day. (name1) laughs harder than (he/she) has all year. Halfway through, (he/she) gets up and dances one dance, just to prove (he/she) can.
